args.query: BIPM definition of the metre speed of light c exact 299792458

observations.content:
[1] Speed of light - Wikipedia
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed_of_light
    It is exact because, by international agreement, a metre is defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1⁄299 792 458 second. The value 299,792,458 metres per second is approximately 1 billion kilometres per hour; 700 million miles per hour.

[2] - metre - BIPM
    https://www.bipm.org/en/si-base-units/metre
    It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum c to be 299 792 458 when expressed in the unit m s–1, where the second is defined in terms of the caesium frequency ΔνCs. This definition implies the exact relation c = 299 792 458 m s –1.

[3] Defining constants - BIPM
    https://www.bipm.org/en/measurement-units/si-defining-constants
    It is by fixing the exact numerical value of each that the unit becomes defined, since the product of the numerical value and the unit must equal the value of the constant.

[4] Speed of Light: Exact Value 299,792,458 m/s
    https://engineeringhulk.com/speed-of-light/
    Oct 15, 2026 · The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 m/s. Values in km/s, km/h and miles/s, speed in water, glass and fibre, history and solved examples.

[5] Speed of Light: Exact Value, Units, Formula & History
    https://physicstribune.com/constants/speed-of-light/
    Oct 15, 2026 · The speed of light in vacuum, c, is exactly 299,792,458 meters per second, about 300,000 kilometers or 186,282 miles every second. The value has no uncertainty because, since 1983, the meter itself has been defined by it.
